hero.title: Evening News & Global Update — Friday 13 November 2026
hero.description: Strait of Hormuz tanker claim, Ukraine peace diplomacy, Nigeria's security debate, the DR Congo Ebola emergency, France's 2027 campaign and global business developments.
hero.marquee: DEVELOPING: Iran reports LNG tanker explosion in Hormuz | Ukraine talks may include Europe | US raises Nigeria security concerns | DR Congo Ebola response under strain | Canada and Angola announce major resource-sector moves

morningSummary: Friday evening's leading story is an Iranian Revolutionary Guards claim that an LNG tanker struck a naval mine and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz. The vessel and any casualties had not been independently confirmed in the reporting available. In Europe, US envoys say the next Ukraine peace talks may include European representatives, while Washington is pursuing a potentially major prisoner exchange. In Nigeria, US officials told Congress that violence against Christian communities remains a serious concern; Abuja has previously rejected Washington's religious-freedom designation and says the country faces terrorism and wider insecurity. The DR Congo Ebola outbreak remains severe, with health workers facing attacks and access constraints. France's National Rally faces questions over the cost of its pension proposals, while the UK debates youth unemployment and welfare reform. Business developments include Canada's proposed C$200 million investment in Woodfibre LNG and Angola's bid for a 10 per cent stake in De Beers. The edition also carries verified jobs, scholarships, grants and training opportunities.
breaking: DEVELOPING / STRAIT OF HORMUZ — Iran's Revolutionary Guards say an LNG tanker struck a naval mine and exploded. Vessel identity, casualties and damage had not been independently confirmed in the report.
UKRAINE — US envoys say European representatives may join the next round of peace talks; Washington is also working towards a potentially large prisoner exchange.
NIGERIA — US officials tell Congress that violence against Christian communities remains a major concern; Nigeria has previously disputed the US designation and framing.
DR CONGO — ECDC reports 11,114 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,433 deaths in the DRC using data up to 10 November; insecurity is obstructing response work.
FRANCE — National Rally is preparing to publish pension proposals amid scrutiny of their fiscal cost.

featured.title: Hormuz Tension Rises After Iran Reports LNG Tanker Explosion
featured.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say an LNG carrier hit a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The ship's identity and casualty details were not immediately available, making independent verification the priority.
featured.content:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on Friday that a tanker carrying liquefied natural gas struck a naval mine and suffered an explosion in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media said the vessel was travelling on what authorities described as an unauthorised and dangerous route. Reuters reported that no immediate details were available about the ship or possible casualties.

The claim comes after Iranian media reported explosions involving four oil tankers in the same waterway on Wednesday and Thursday. The strait is a critical route for global oil and gas shipments, and repeated incidents have raised concern among ship operators, insurers and energy-importing countries.

WHY IT MATTERS: Any sustained disruption could raise freight and insurance costs, delay energy cargoes and add volatility to oil and gas prices. The effect would reach import-dependent economies, including countries already facing pressure on foreign exchange and public finances.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Independent confirmation of the vessel's identity, its flag, ownership, damage, crew safety and the precise location will be essential. Watch for statements from maritime authorities, ship operators and regional governments. The Iranian account remains an attributed claim, not an independently verified finding.
featured.source: Reuters; Iranian Revolutionary Guards statements; maritime-security reporting

topStories.title: Putin Signals European Role in Next Ukraine Talks as Washington Pursues Major Prisoner Exchange
topStories.summary: US envoys say European representatives could join the next round of negotiations, while Jared Kushner says Washington is working towards a potentially large prisoner exchange.
topStories.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed in principle to European representatives joining the next round of Ukraine peace talks, according to comments by US envoy Steve Witkoff after meetings in Moscow. The development follows US envoys' contacts with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Jared Kushner said the United States was also working towards what could become the largest prisoner exchange of the war, potentially allowing thousands of people to return to their families. He did not provide a timetable or the terms under discussion.

European participation matters because any settlement would directly affect the continent's security, sanctions policy, reconstruction commitments and future guarantees for Ukraine. However, agreement to attend talks does not mean that Moscow and Kyiv have reached agreement on territory, security arrangements or a ceasefire.

WHY IT MATTERS: A credible process needs Ukraine's participation and a meaningful European role, while prisoner exchanges can provide humanitarian progress even when wider political differences remain unresolved.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for confirmation of the next meeting, the composition of the European delegation and any formal announcement on prisoner lists or exchange arrangements.
topStories.source: Reuters reporting carried by AnewZ; statements by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner

topStories.title: Washington Says Violence Against Christian Communities Remains a Major Concern in Nigeria
topStories.summary: US officials told Congress that attacks continue, while Nigeria has previously rejected Washington's religious-freedom designation and says the country faces terrorism and wider insecurity.
topStories.content:
The US State Department says violence affecting Christian communities in Nigeria remains a major concern, a year after the Trump administration designated the country a 'country of particular concern' over religious freedom. Assistant Secretary Frank Garcia told a congressional panel that Washington is working with Nigerian authorities and wants perpetrators held accountable.

Nigeria has rejected the designation as based on misinformation and has argued that the country is confronting terrorism, banditry, kidnappings and communal violence rather than a single pattern of religious persecution. Nigerian officials have said they would welcome cooperation with the United States provided Nigeria's sovereignty and territorial integrity are respected.

The debate comes as insecurity remains a major issue ahead of the January 2027 elections. Violence in the Middle Belt, insurgency in the north-east, banditry and kidnappings require responses that protect all communities and address the different causes of conflict.

WHY IT MATTERS: The issue affects Nigeria's international relations, security cooperation and domestic political debate. Accurate reporting must recognise attacks on Christian communities without erasing Muslim victims or the wider pattern of insecurity.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for a formal response from Abuja, evidence of measurable security improvements, and details of any new US-Nigeria cooperation. Statements by officials should be assessed alongside independently verified incident data.
topStories.source: Reuters; US State Department; statements previously made by the Nigerian government

topStories.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Remains Severe as Attacks on Health Workers Disrupt Response
topStories.summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reports 11,114 confirmed cases and 5,433 deaths in DR Congo as of 11 November; insecurity is obstructing outbreak control.
topStories.content:
The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains a major public-health emergency. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 11,114 confirmed cases and 5,433 related deaths in the DRC using data up to 10 November. Eight provinces have been affected.

The response is being weakened by insecurity. Africa CDC has warned that armed attacks, assaults on responders and damage to health facilities are limiting access to communities. Reuters reporting on the agency's briefing said more than 1,000 contacts had been lost to follow-up and three confirmed cases remained unaccounted for.

The ECDC also reported one Ebola case in Nigeria in October involving a person with travel history to Uganda who was medically evacuated to Switzerland. The agency said 62 contacts had been identified. This information should not be misrepresented as evidence of wider transmission in Nigeria.

WHY IT MATTERS: Contact tracing, safe treatment, community trust and access for health workers are central to stopping transmission. Violence can reverse progress and increase risks across borders.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch updates from the DRC health authorities, WHO, Africa CDC and ECDC, especially changes in case numbers, contact tracing and safe access to affected areas.
topStories.source: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control; Africa CDC; Reuters; WHO

topStories.title: Marine Le Pen Faces Questions over the Cost of National Rally Pension Promises
topStories.summary: The National Rally is preparing to present its pension proposals as it seeks to convince voters and investors that its programme can be financed.
topStories.content:
Marine Le Pen's National Rally is preparing to set out its pension proposals ahead of France's 2027 presidential election, amid questions about the cost of reversing parts of Emmanuel Macron's pension reform. Reuters reports that Le Pen has promised to allow some workers who began their careers early to retire at 60, while the party is working to show how its programme could be funded.

Pensions are one of France's largest areas of public spending. The debate is therefore not only about the retirement age but also about contribution periods, eligibility, the public budget and the distribution of costs between workers, employers and taxpayers. The party's proposals have attracted scrutiny because reversing the existing reform could add substantial annual costs, while its wider savings targets would need to be specified and tested.

WHY IT MATTERS: Pension policy affects millions of workers and retirees and can influence France's borrowing needs, labour supply and public finances. Election promises should be assessed against detailed costing rather than slogans.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The National Rally is expected to present more detail next Tuesday. Watch for independent fiscal assessments, eligibility rules and the party's explanation of how it would pay for the changes.
topStories.source: Reuters; French public-finance and pension-policy data

topStories.title: UK Weighs Welfare Changes as Youth Unemployment Becomes a Political Pressure Point
topStories.summary: The government is considering welfare changes amid concern about rising youth unemployment, with the debate focusing on how to improve access to work and training.
topStories.content:
The UK is facing renewed debate over youth unemployment and the role of welfare policy. Reuters reports that the government is considering changes to welfare arrangements as it responds to a rise in the number of young people who are not in employment, education or training.

The policy challenge is broader than benefit rules. Young people can face barriers including limited work experience, skills mismatches, poor access to transport, health needs and a shortage of suitable entry-level vacancies. Employers and public services will be central to whether training routes lead to sustained jobs.

WHY IT MATTERS: Long periods outside work or education can affect earnings, health and future productivity. A policy focused only on reducing benefits may fail if it does not create realistic routes into employment.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the government's detailed proposals, any expansion of apprenticeships and technical education, and evidence that public-sector recruitment plans translate into paid opportunities.
topStories.source: Reuters; UK government employment and labour-market data

topStories.title: EU Leaders Use First Dedicated AI Summit to Address Europe's Technology Gap
topStories.summary: At a summit in Dublin, EU leaders are discussing investment, regulation and the infrastructure needed to compete with the United States and China in artificial intelligence.
topStories.content:
European Union leaders met in Dublin for the bloc's first dedicated summit on artificial intelligence. Reuters reports that the discussion is focused on how Europe can close the gap with the United States and China while addressing investment, regulation and safety.

The challenge includes access to advanced chips, data centres, energy, skilled workers and finance. Europe's Chips Act and plans for AI gigafactories are intended to strengthen the region's capacity, but funding disagreements and slow implementation remain obstacles. Leaders are also weighing how to protect the public while allowing companies to develop and deploy new systems.

WHY IT MATTERS: AI capability is increasingly linked to industrial productivity, public services, defence and economic sovereignty. Dependence on a small number of overseas providers can expose Europe to commercial and strategic risks.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for investment commitments, progress on shared computing infrastructure and proposals to simplify rules without weakening safeguards.

topStories.title: Strike on Nasser Hospital Kills Six, Including a Doctor and a Child, Gaza Health Ministry Says
topStories.summary: An Israeli strike hit the hospital's surgical wing in Khan Younis, according to Gaza health authorities; Israel said it targeted militants, while hospital staff reported severe damage.
topStories.content:
A strike hit the surgical wing of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis shortly after midnight on Thursday, killing six people, including a doctor and a 13-year-old boy, according to Gaza's Health Ministry and Associated Press reporting. At least 28 people were reported wounded. Hospital officials and medical staff described damage to operating rooms and wards.

Israel said it had targeted a Hamas commander and other militants, alleging that Hamas had established a presence at the site. Hospital staff and a British volunteer surgeon said there had been no warning. The claims about the military target and the circumstances of the strike require independent scrutiny.

The incident adds pressure to an already fragile health system, where shortages of medical supplies and damage to facilities have reduced the availability of specialist care.

WHY IT MATTERS: Hospitals and medical personnel are protected under international humanitarian law, subject to specific legal conditions. Any allegation of military use of a hospital and any attack on medical facilities require careful investigation.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for independent investigations, further information about the alleged target, casualty updates and whether hospital services can resume.
topStories.source: Associated Press; Gaza Health Ministry; Israeli military statements; medical staff accounts

topStories.title: Canada Plans C$200 Million Investment to Expand Woodfibre LNG Project Capacity
topStories.summary: A Reuters report says the federal government plans to invest C$200 million in the British Columbia LNG project as Canada seeks to expand export capacity.
topStories.content:
Canada is preparing to invest C$200 million in the Woodfibre LNG project in British Columbia to support an expansion of its capacity, Reuters reported, citing a source. The project is part of Canada's wider effort to increase its role in global liquefied natural gas markets and diversify energy exports.

LNG investment can bring construction activity, export revenue and potential access to new markets, but it also raises questions about costs, Indigenous consultation, environmental impacts and the long-term demand for fossil fuels as countries pursue energy-transition targets.

WHY IT MATTERS: The decision connects Canada's industrial strategy with global energy security and competition for LNG supply. It may also affect trade relationships with Asian buyers.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for an official government announcement, project financing details, construction milestones and environmental or regulatory conditions.
topStories.source: Reuters; Canadian government and project information

topStories.title: Angola Seeks 10% Stake in De Beers as Ownership Talks Reshape Diamond Industry
topStories.summary: Angola is seeking a minority stake in De Beers as Anglo American plans its exit, in a move that could increase African producer influence over the diamond business.
topStories.content:
Angola is seeking a 10 per cent stake in De Beers as Anglo American moves forward with plans to exit the diamond company, Reuters reported. The move reflects the interest of diamond-producing countries in securing a greater role in the ownership and value chain of the industry.

For Angola, a stake could offer influence over marketing, investment and the future direction of one of the world's best-known diamond businesses. The wider negotiations will involve questions of valuation, financing, governance and the position of other potential investors.

WHY IT MATTERS: Resource-producing countries are increasingly seeking more value from their minerals rather than relying only on extraction and export. The outcome could influence investment and bargaining power across southern Africa's diamond sector.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for formal proposals, financing arrangements and the response of Anglo American and other stakeholders. A request for a stake is not yet a completed transaction.
topStories.source: Reuters; Angolan government statements; Anglo American corporate information

topStories.title: Trump, Putin and Xi Expected at APEC as Attention Turns to Strategic Rivalries and Trade
topStories.summary: The 21-member APEC gathering in Shenzhen next week is expected to draw major attention because the leaders of the United States, Russia and China may attend.
topStories.content:
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum is preparing for a high-profile gathering in Shenzhen next week, with US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping among the leaders expected to attend, according to Reuters. The 21-member forum focuses on trade and economic cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region.

The meeting will take place amid trade tensions, technology competition, energy-security concerns and disputes over regional security. Any direct contacts among the three leaders would attract attention, but attendance at the same summit does not itself signal a bilateral agreement.

WHY IT MATTERS: APEC economies account for a substantial share of global trade and production. Decisions or signals on tariffs, supply chains, technology and investment can affect businesses well beyond the region.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the final attendance list, bilateral meeting schedules and any joint statements on trade, investment or regional stability.
topStories.source: Reuters; APEC background information; official summit announcements

leadersWatch.title: Leaders Watch
leadersWatch.description: Profiles of political and institutional leaders whose decisions are shaping international affairs. Reports distinguish confirmed decisions from political statements, allegations and unresolved legal questions.

leaders.name: Donald Trump
leaders.headline: US diplomacy on Ukraine and Iran keeps Washington at the centre of global security debates
leaders.report: US envoys have met Vladimir Putin and then Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Washington seeks to restart Ukraine negotiations. The administration is also maintaining its blockade on Iranian oil shipments.
leaders.background: The administration is balancing diplomatic efforts, military commitments, energy security and domestic economic pressures.
leaders.implications: The credibility of US diplomacy will depend on whether talks produce humanitarian progress and reduce escalation risks.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Statements from all parties should be tested against confirmed agreements, implementation and independently verified developments.
leaders.source: Associated Press; Reuters; White House statements

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.headline: France balances European security leadership with domestic economic and social pressures
leaders.report: France is participating in European discussions on Ukraine and continental security while the government faces continuing public debate over wages, purchasing power and social policy.
leaders.background: The domestic debate is unfolding ahead of the 2027 presidential contest and amid pressure on public finances.
leaders.implications: France's influence in Europe depends on both diplomatic engagement and domestic political stability.
leaders.radiantWavesView: International leadership should be considered alongside measurable progress on household costs, public services and economic confidence.

leaders.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
leaders.headline: 2027 election preparations face scrutiny over funding, technology and legal disputes
leaders.report: INEC says it will test accreditation and electronic result transmission in a nationwide mock exercise on 28 November. The commission also says it is dealing with more than 300 pending court cases.
leaders.background: The electoral process includes disputes over party leadership, voter-register concerns, election funding and security.
leaders.implications: Public confidence will depend on transparent procedures, timely funding and equal application of the law.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will assess government and opposition claims against official records, court decisions and verifiable electoral safeguards.

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.headline: INEC says Atiku's eligibility will be governed by binding court decisions
leaders.report: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission is constitutionally required to obey court orders concerning Atiku's eligibility and the ADC leadership dispute.
leaders.background: The dispute remains within the legal process. ADC has criticised aspects of the judgment timeline and says it will pursue lawful remedies.
leaders.implications: The INEC statement is not a final judicial determination of Atiku's eligibility. The outcome depends on the courts and the applicable electoral law.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Coverage must distinguish party allegations, legal arguments and final court decisions; no outcome should be assumed before it is delivered.
leaders.source: The Guardian Nigeria; Channels Television; INEC

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.headline: Canada joins European partners in discussions on Ukraine and security
leaders.report: Canada's prime minister is among leaders attending the Dublin European Political Community summit, with Canada also expected at next week's APEC leaders' meeting in China.
leaders.background: Canada's diplomacy spans transatlantic security, trade, climate and Indo-Pacific partnerships.
leaders.implications: Ottawa's choices will influence cooperation between North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific economies.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Watch for concrete Canadian commitments on Ukraine, trade resilience and regional security rather than summit statements alone.

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.headline: Putin meets US envoys but core Ukraine demands remain unresolved
leaders.report: Putin met US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow. Discussions followed Abu Dhabi talks that produced agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but no peace breakthrough.
leaders.background: Russia continues to oppose European troops in Ukraine and maintains territorial claims rejected by Kyiv and its partners.
leaders.implications: Moscow's position will shape whether negotiations move beyond limited humanitarian arrangements.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Any settlement should be judged by its terms, implementation and respect for Ukraine's sovereignty and international law.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.headline: China prepares to host APEC leaders in Shenzhen next week
leaders.report: Xi Jinping is expected to chair the APEC leaders' meeting on 18–19 November, with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin among the leaders expected to attend.
leaders.background: The summit will take place amid technology competition, trade tensions, supply-chain concerns and regional security issues.
leaders.implications: The meeting could influence trade expectations and the tone of US-China engagement, although APEC commitments are voluntary and consensus-based.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Watch for confirmed bilateral meetings and specific commitments; attendance alone does not establish a diplomatic breakthrough.

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leaders.headline: Zelenskyy seeks meaningful European participation in the next Ukraine talks
leaders.report: Zelenskyy met US envoys in Dublin after their meeting with Putin. He said Europe should have a seat within the next negotiating team, not merely participate separately.
leaders.background: Ukraine continues to reject Russian demands over occupied territory and seeks credible long-term security guarantees.
leaders.implications: The negotiating format will affect the legitimacy and durability of any future settlement.
leaders.radiantWavesView: A durable peace requires Ukraine's meaningful participation, verifiable commitments and protection of civilian security.

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.headline: EU leaders press for a stronger European role in Ukraine diplomacy
leaders.report: The European Commission president met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Dublin ahead of next week's UK-EU summit, while European leaders discussed Ukraine and continental security.
leaders.background: The EU is balancing support for Ukraine with defence coordination, trade relations and resilience against hybrid threats.
leaders.implications: The next summit will show whether European governments can turn broad commitments into practical policy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Proposals should be assessed by their funding, implementation timetable and measurable effect on security and trade.

leaders.name: Andy Burnham
leaders.position: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.headline: UK seeks a practical reset in relations with the European Union
leaders.report: Burnham met Ursula von der Leyen in Dublin and said the UK-EU summit planned for next week could help reduce red tape and costs for businesses and consumers.
leaders.background: The proposed cooperation remains under negotiation and must still be translated into an agreed package.
leaders.implications: A workable UK-EU deal could affect trade, investment, regulatory cooperation and opportunities for young people.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The public should judge the talks by the final text and the practical effects on businesses, prices and mobility.

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.headline: African public-health coordination remains vital as insecurity disrupts Ebola response
leaders.report: Africa CDC says attacks on health workers and facilities are undermining containment efforts in eastern DR Congo.
leaders.background: The response requires safe access, contact tracing, community trust and sustained regional coordination.
leaders.implications: The outbreak demonstrates how conflict can undermine health security across borders.
leaders.radiantWavesView: African governments and regional institutions should prioritise safe access for health teams, transparent data and sustained support for affected communities.

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.headline: French opposition parties position themselves as social tensions shape the 2027 debate
leaders.report: The cost-of-living debate and continuing talks between the government, unions and employers are likely to shape the political environment ahead of the next presidential election.
leaders.background: Economic policy, public services, immigration and national identity remain central themes in French political competition.
leaders.implications: The evolving debate may influence the direction of French domestic and European policy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will distinguish confirmed candidacies and legal developments from campaign speculation and political claims.

opportunities.eligibility: Nigerian applicants with at least a Second Class Upper degree obtained within the previous five years and completed NYSC, subject to the full programme rules.

opportunities.title: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship — 2027 campaign
opportunities.organisation: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs / Campus France
opportunities.description: Scholarships for outstanding international students applying for master's and doctoral programmes at French higher-education institutions. Candidates must be nominated by a French institution; applicants do not submit directly to Campus France.
opportunities.eligibility: Master's applicants must be under 29; doctoral applicants under 35 under the 2027 programme rules. French institutions set earlier internal deadlines, so contact the intended institution promptly.

opportunities.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027/2028
opportunities.organisation: Swiss Confederation / Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students
opportunities.description: Scholarships primarily for early-career researchers from abroad who have already completed a master's degree. The programme is open to applicants from 183 countries, but country-specific procedures and deadlines apply.
opportunities.eligibility: Mainly early-career researchers with a completed master's degree. Applicants must confirm that their nationality and research proposal are eligible and check the deadline with the Swiss representation responsible for their country.
opportunities.deadline: Country-specific — verify with the Swiss representation

opportunities.title: USPF Changemaker Challenge 2026
opportunities.description: Digital-inclusion challenge for innovation teams and early-stage startups developing ICT solutions in agriculture, education, healthcare, financial inclusion or clean energy. National prizes: ₦5 million for first place, ₦3 million for second and ₦2 million for third; finalists also receive incubation support.
opportunities.eligibility: Teams and early-stage startups with practical ICT solutions for underserved communities. Review the challenge rules and submit through the official application platform.

opportunities.title: Young Africa Innovates — Cohort 2
opportunities.location: Abia, Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Katsina, Niger, Plateau and Taraba, Nigeria
opportunities.description: Youth-led innovation programme offering capacity support, bootcamp, incubation, mentorship and potential grant support for ventures addressing real problems in participating states.
opportunities.eligibility: Applicants must be aged 18–35 and resident in one of the seven listed states. Any sector is welcome; reviewers assess problem relevance, proof of concept, scalability and community impact.

opportunities.title: Global EbA Fund — Medium-Size Grants
opportunities.location: Global — ODA-eligible countries, including eligible African contexts
opportunities.description: Grants of up to US$500,000 for innovative, collaborative ecosystem-based adaptation projects. Projects may run for up to 24 months and must address climate resilience, scaling, policy, evidence or investment barriers. The official closing time is 16 November 2026 at 23:59 Pacific Standard Time (17 November at 08:59 Central European Time).
opportunities.eligibility: Legally recognised NGOs, INGOs, community organisations, universities, research institutes, private-sector organisations and consortia. Projects must meet the Fund's EbA criteria, work with local partners and build on existing work. Not an individual scholarship or general business grant.

opportunities.title: 3MTT Delivery Network — Cohort 5 Partner and Funding Applications
opportunities.organisation: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Nigeria
opportunities.description: Registered training organisations can apply for results-based funding to train digital and technical talent. Organisations that do not train can register interest as Opportunity, Funding, Capability, Research and Data, State and Agency, or Amplification Partners.
opportunities.eligibility: For funded delivery-partner applications, the lead must be registered and operating in Nigeria, have recent training delivery evidence and capacity to train at least 100 fellows within six months. RadiantWaves as a media organisation would be more appropriately considered for the Amplification Partner pathway unless it works with an eligible training-provider consortium.

todaysBigQuestion: How can African governments strengthen public security and public-health systems while protecting civil liberties, community trust and national sovereignty?
thoughtForToday: A credible public response begins with facts: acknowledge what is known, identify what remains uncertain, and act before uncertainty becomes a crisis.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: RadiantWaves Perspective: Security Requires Evidence, Trust and Accountability
radiantWavesPerspective.content: Today's developments underline how quickly security risks cross borders. The Strait of Hormuz matters to global energy supply; insecurity in eastern DR Congo is obstructing an urgent public-health response; and Nigeria's security challenges are drawing renewed international scrutiny. Governments should cooperate where interests align, but policy must be based on transparent evidence, protection of civilians and accountability. In reporting allegations or official claims, RadiantWaves will distinguish what has been independently confirmed from what remains disputed.
